universe.name: Marvel: Your Universe
universe.description: A curated, fixed-timeline Marvel continuity where real-world present day is in-universe present day. This is built like a wiki first — character files with the baseline facts — with curated stories layered in over time. Cherry-picked, but additive: everything currently in this file is canon, something that actually happened here. Nothing is a hypothetical alternate to pick between. The only way something leaves is an explicit retcon, not by default.

timelineAnchor.note: Real time = story time. Update currentYear each year, or compute it in js/app.js from Date(). The timeline only tracks big, universe-level moments (team formations, origins, major story beats) — not every character needs a point on it. Same-year moments stack into a single point instead of spreading across several.

characters.name: Tony Stark
characters.bioShort: Genius inventor and CEO of Stark Industries who built a suit of powered armor to survive captivity, then kept building.
characters.bioLong: A billionaire engineer whose weapons-manufacturing background gave way to a career protecting the people his old tech used to endanger. Builds and rebuilds his armor constantly, treating each new Iron Man suit as a running answer to the last threat he barely survived. A founding member and frequent financier of the Avengers.

characters.name: Steve Rogers
characters.bioShort: Recipient of the Super Soldier Serum and a founding Avenger, defined by an old-fashioned sense of duty.
characters.bioLong: A frail volunteer transformed by an experimental serum into the peak of human ability, and trained to lead. His service with the Howling Commandos is part of the record, though how a WWII-era origin squares with this universe's real-time-equals-story-time premise is still an open question worth pinning down. Carries a vibranium shield and leads by example more than by rank.

characters.name: Thor Odinson
characters.bioShort: Asgardian god of thunder, wielder of the enchanted hammer Mjolnir, and a founding Avenger.
characters.bioLong: Crown prince of Asgard, banished to Earth to learn humility before being deemed worthy again of his hammer. Superhumanly strong and durable, and able to summon storms and fly by Mjolnir's power. How much of Asgardian myth and politics stays in play on a grounded modern timeline is still to be decided.

characters.name: Clint Barton
characters.bioShort: World-class marksman with no powers beyond relentless skill and nerve — a founding Avenger.
characters.bioLong: A former circus performer and S.H.I.E.L.D. operative who never stopped being the best shot in the room. Fights alongside gods and monsters using nothing but a bow, a quiver of trick arrows, and total confidence in his aim.

characters.name: Natasha Romanoff
characters.bioShort: Former espionage operative turned Avenger, and one of the team's founding members.
characters.bioLong: Trained from a young age as a spy and assassin before defecting West and putting that training to work for S.H.I.E.L.D. and later the Avengers. No superpowers — just world-class combat training, tradecraft, and an ability to read a room (or a lie) instantly.

characters.name: Bruce Banner
characters.bioShort: A gamma-radiation accident left Bruce Banner unable to control a second, monstrous identity.
characters.bioLong: A brilliant physicist whose gamma-radiation experiment went wrong, leaving him able to transform — usually under stress or anger — into the Hulk: a towering, superhumanly strong engine of destruction with limited impulse control. Banner spends as much energy trying to prevent the transformation as the Avengers spend being glad he doesn't.

characters.name: Ant-Man
characters.bioShort: A founding-era Avenger who can shrink to insect size without losing his strength.
characters.bioLong: Uses size-changing technology to shrink down to insect scale while keeping full-size strength, and can communicate with and control ants. Whose civilian identity this is on this timeline — Hank Pym, Scott Lang, or someone else — is still an open call.

characters.name: Wasp
characters.bioShort: A founding-era Avenger who shares Ant-Man's size-changing technology, with flight and energy blasts of her own.
characters.bioLong: Shrinks to insect size like Ant-Man, but adds wings and bioelectric "stings" to the mix. Whose civilian identity this is on this timeline — Janet van Dyne, Hope van Dyne, or someone else — is still an open call.

characters.name: Peter Parker
characters.bioShort: Bitten by a radioactive/genetically-modified spider as a teenager — a newer hero than the founding Avengers.
characters.bioLong: Gains wall-crawling, superhuman strength and agility, and a precognitive "spider-sense" at 16, and builds his own web-shooters rather than producing webbing naturally. Tonally, his corner of the universe plays like the '90s animated series: a rotating rogues gallery, a supporting cast that matters, and consequences that stick. Later wears an alien symbiote suit for a time before rejecting it — see Venom.

characters.name: Johnny Storm
characters.bioShort: The youngest member of the Fantastic Four, able to engulf himself in flame and fly.
characters.bioLong: Gained his powers alongside Sue, Reed, and Ben in the cosmic-ray accident that created the Fantastic Four. Can ignite his entire body without harm, fly under his own power, and throw fireballs — the most overtly showy of the team's powerset, matched by the most impulsive personality.

characters.name: Susan Storm
characters.bioShort: Founding member of the Fantastic Four, able to turn invisible and generate protective force fields.
characters.bioLong: Gained her powers in the same cosmic-ray accident as her brother Johnny, Reed Richards, and Ben Grimm. Can render herself and others invisible and project nearly indestructible force fields — often the team's most tactically versatile member despite the least flashy power.

characters.name: Reed Richards
characters.bioShort: Leader and chief scientist of the Fantastic Four, able to stretch his body into nearly any shape.
characters.bioLong: The scientist whose experimental spacecraft was hit by cosmic rays, giving his crew their powers and himself the ability to stretch, twist, and flatten his entire body like elastic. Widely regarded as one of the smartest people on Earth, and leads the Fantastic Four accordingly.

characters.name: Ben Grimm
characters.bioShort: Founding member of the Fantastic Four, transformed into a super-strong, rock-skinned powerhouse.
characters.bioLong: Reed Richards' best friend and the pilot of the spacecraft that gave the Fantastic Four their powers — in his case, superhuman strength and durability at the cost of a permanent rock-like hide. The team's muscle and its conscience in roughly equal measure.

characters.name: Scott Summers
characters.bioShort: Field leader of the X-Men, who fires concussive force blasts from his eyes that he can only control through a ruby-quartz visor.
characters.bioLong: One of the X-Men's founding members and its de facto field leader — disciplined nearly to a fault, which makes him a natural tactician and a difficult person to get close to. His optic blasts are effectively uncontrollable without his visor or glasses.

characters.name: Logan
characters.bioShort: Healing-factor mutant with retractable bone claws, a long and murky past, and a short temper.
characters.bioLong: A mutant with an accelerated healing factor, enhanced senses, and retractable claws — augmented further by an unbreakable metal skeleton grafted on without his consent. How much of his classic decades-spanning backstory stays canon on a fixed real-time timeline is still an open call.

characters.name: Jean Grey
characters.bioShort: Founding X-Man with powerful telepathy and telekinesis, periodically overtaken by a cosmic force called the Phoenix.
characters.bioLong: One of the X-Men's founding members, gifted with telepathy and telekinesis that grow more powerful — and more dangerous — when she bonds with the cosmic Phoenix Force. That bond has a history of ending badly; how much of that arc plays out here is still unwritten.

characters.name: Remy LeBeau
characters.bioShort: Cajun mutant who charges objects with explosive kinetic energy, favoring a deck of playing cards as throwing weapons.
characters.bioLong: A former professional thief recruited into the X-Men, able to charge any object he touches with volatile kinetic energy and detonate it on contact — most famously a thrown, glowing playing card. Charming, cagey about his past, and good at both.

characters.name: Max Eisenhardt
characters.bioShort: Master of magnetism and mutant supremacist, alternately the X-Men's greatest enemy and an uneasy ally.
characters.bioLong: A Holocaust survivor whose mutant power to generate and control magnetic fields makes him one of the most dangerous beings on Earth. Founded the Brotherhood of Mutants to fight for mutantkind by force where Charles Xavier preferred diplomacy — a philosophical rift, not a personal one, since the two were once close friends.

characters.name: Eddie Brock
characters.bioShort: A journalist rival of Peter Parker's who bonds with the alien symbiote after Spider-Man rejects it.
characters.bioLong: Eddie Brock's own downfall — a ruined story, a public humiliation, whatever's on record — is still unwritten. What's set: the symbiote Peter discarded found Eddie, who, unlike Peter, bonded with it willingly and let it take hold. The result is Venom: spider-powers, no restraint, and a fixation on destroying the man who rejected the very thing that made him.

characters.name: Cletus Kasady
characters.bioShort: A spawn of Eddie Brock's symbiote, bonded directly to a violent serial killer. Considerably less restrained than Venom.
characters.bioLong: The specifics of Kasady and Brock's overlap are still unwritten. What's set: a spawn of the Venom symbiote bonds directly to Cletus Kasady's bloodstream, making the two inseparable in a way even Eddie and his symbiote aren't. Meaner, redder, and far less interested in restraint.

characters.name: Ben Reilly
characters.bioShort: One of two clones of Peter Parker created by Norman Osborn, who grew into his own identity rather than replacing Peter.
characters.bioLong: Created alongside Kaine in Norman Osborn's cloning experiment. Unlike the classic Clone Saga, this doesn't spiral into a years-long identity crisis — Ben mostly just helps, stepping in for Peter when he's overwhelmed or needs to be two places at once. The two ended up with something like a brotherly bond instead of a rivalry.

characters.name: Kaine
characters.bioShort: The other of Norman Osborn's two Peter Parker clones — a rougher, less resolved arc than Ben's.
characters.bioLong: Created in the same experiment that produced Ben Reilly, but Kaine's cloning was less stable and his path since has been rougher and less resolved. Where his loyalties and identity settle is still unwritten.

characters.name: Norman Osborn
characters.bioShort: Industrialist, Oscorp CEO, and Spider-Man's archenemy — under two separate costumed identities.
characters.bioLong: A ruthless industrialist who runs Oscorp by day and has, at different points, operated as both the Green Goblin and Iron Patriot. Also responsible for cloning Peter Parker, producing Ben Reilly and Kaine. See his linked identities for the costumed history.

characters.name: Norman Osborn
characters.bioShort: Norman Osborn's original, and most infamous, costumed identity — Spider-Man's archenemy.
characters.bioLong: Osborn's alter ego: a bladed glider, pumpkin bombs, and a personal vendetta against Spider-Man that outlasts every other rivalry in Peter's life. See Norman Osborn for the person underneath the mask, and Iron Patriot for the identity he takes up later.

characters.name: Norman Osborn
characters.bioShort: A weaponized, Stark-tech-inspired suit of armor Norman Osborn wears while presenting himself as a hero.
characters.bioLong: PLACEHOLDER — the specifics of when and why Osborn takes up this identity (and how it relates to Stark's own armor) are still unwritten. What's set: it's the same man as Green Goblin and Norman Osborn, wearing a very different face to the public.

characters.name: Otto Octavius
characters.bioShort: Brilliant, unstable physicist fused with four mechanical arms after a lab accident.
characters.bioLong: A respected nuclear physicist whose four mechanical, mind-linked arms fused permanently to his spine in a lab accident — one that also unbalanced him psychologically. Every bit Spider-Man's intellectual equal, and far less restrained.

characters.name: Adrian Toomes
characters.bioShort: Aging engineer with a flight harness and a grudge.
characters.bioLong: An engineer who built a flight harness that gives him strength, speed, and razor-taloned gloves to match — and used it to go straight to crime rather than retire quietly. Part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

characters.name: Quentin Beck
characters.bioShort: Special-effects expert turned illusionist supervillain.
characters.bioLong: A former Hollywood stuntman and special-effects wizard who turned elaborate illusions, smoke, and misdirection into a criminal career — and a genuine threat to anyone who trusts their own eyes. Part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

characters.name: Flint Marko
characters.bioShort: Career criminal turned into living sand by a freak accident.
characters.bioLong: A small-time crook caught in an experimental radiation test at a beach, leaving him able to turn his body to sand, reshape it at will, and absorb blunt force with ease. Part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

characters.name: Sergei Kravinoff
characters.bioShort: Big-game hunter obsessed with proving himself against Spider-Man.
characters.bioLong: A Russian nobleman turned world-class big-game hunter, enhanced by mystical herbal potions that give him superhuman strength, speed, and senses. Considers Spider-Man the ultimate quarry — a matter of pride more than money. Part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

characters.name: Aleksei Sytsevich
characters.bioShort: Powered armor grafted to his body, brute force over strategy.
characters.bioLong: A career criminal who volunteered for an experimental process bonding a nearly indestructible armored hide to his body, granting immense strength and durability at the cost of subtlety. Part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

characters.name: Max Dillon
characters.bioShort: Electrical accident left him able to generate and control electricity.
characters.bioLong: A lineman caught in a freak electrical accident that rewrote his body's relationship to electricity — he generates, channels, and rides bolts of it at will. Part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

characters.name: Curt Connors
characters.bioShort: Scientist whose reptilian regeneration formula cost him control of himself.
characters.bioLong: A brilliant herpetologist who lost an arm and, in trying to regrow it with a reptile-derived serum, transformed into a hyper-intelligent, savage reptilian creature. One of Spider-Man's more tragic rogues — Connors himself is rarely the one in control.

characters.name: Dmitri Smerdyakov
characters.bioShort: Master of disguise and identity theft.
characters.bioLong: A trained infiltrator whose gift for disguise and mimicry lets him impersonate almost anyone, physically and behaviorally, long enough to do serious damage before anyone notices the swap. Part of Spider-Man's rogues gallery.

characters.name: Herman Schultz
characters.bioShort: Safecracker turned supervillain, armed with a pair of vibro-shock gauntlets of his own design.
characters.bioLong: A career criminal and engineer who built a pair of gauntlets that fire concussive vibro-blasts, and a padded suit to absorb the recoil. More pragmatic than most of Spider-Man's rogues — prefers a payday to a grudge.

characters.name: Mary Jane Watson
characters.bioShort: Peter Parker's on-and-off love interest and closest confidant.
characters.bioLong: A childhood neighbor of Peter's who grows into his most enduring relationship — sharp, unshakeable under pressure, and one of the few people who eventually knows exactly who he is under the mask.

characters.name: Gwen Stacy
characters.bioShort: Classmate and early love interest of Peter Parker's.
characters.bioLong: PLACEHOLDER — decide her arc here. In the classic comics her story ends tragically at the Green Goblin's hands; whether that beat happens on this timeline is still an open call.

characters.name: May Parker
characters.bioShort: Peter Parker's aunt and guardian.
characters.bioLong: Raised Peter after the death of his parents alongside her husband Ben. PLACEHOLDER — how much she knows about Spider-Man, and when she finds out, is still an open call.

characters.name: Harry Osborn
characters.bioShort: Peter Parker's best friend and Norman Osborn's son — caught in the middle of his father's double life.
characters.bioLong: PLACEHOLDER — decide whether he ever takes up a Goblin identity of his own here, as he does in the source comics, or stays out of the mask entirely.

characters.name: J. Jonah Jameson
characters.bioShort: Daily Bugle publisher, perpetually convinced Spider-Man is a menace.
characters.bioLong: Runs the Daily Bugle with a permanent grudge against Spider-Man, whom he considers a vigilante menace rather than a hero — and happens to be Peter's sometime employer as a freelance photographer, with no idea who's really behind the camera.

characters.name: Matt Murdock
characters.bioShort: Blind attorney by day, vigilante by night.
characters.bioLong: Blinded as a boy in an accident that also heightened his remaining senses to superhuman levels, giving him a radar-like sense of his surroundings. Practices law by day and cleans up Hell's Kitchen by night with a billy club and gymnast's reflexes.

characters.name: Frank Castle
characters.bioShort: A one-man war on organized crime, armed and utterly without the restraint most heroes hold onto.
characters.bioLong: A former Marine whose family was killed in mob crossfire, after which he traded any interest in due process for a skull-emblazoned vest and an arsenal. No powers — just training, guns, and a body count most heroes would call a war crime.

characters.name: Luke Cage
characters.bioShort: Wrongly imprisoned man turned bulletproof, superhumanly strong powerhouse.
characters.bioLong: Framed and imprisoned, Cage volunteered for an experimental procedure that left him with steel-hard, near-invulnerable skin and superhuman strength — and broke him out in the process. Works Harlem's streets as hired muscle with a conscience.

characters.name: Eric Brooks
characters.bioShort: Vampire hunter, born with most of a vampire's strengths and none of its weaknesses.
characters.bioLong: Born to a mother bitten during his delivery, Blade carries a dhampir's enhanced strength, speed, and healing, along with immunity to most vampiric weaknesses — and has spent his life hunting the thing that made him. Whether the supernatural side of this universe is fully in play is still an open call.

characters.name: Johnny Blaze
characters.bioShort: Bonded to the Spirit of Vengeance, becoming a flaming-skulled avenger of the wronged.
characters.bioLong: A motorcycle stuntman who made a deal to save a life and ended up bonded to a demonic Spirit of Vengeance — transforming, when needed, into a fire-skulled rider whose chain and "penance stare" punish the guilty. Whether the supernatural side of this universe is fully in play is still an open call.

characters.name: Danny Rand
characters.bioShort: Master martial artist wielding the mystical power of the Iron Fist.
characters.bioLong: Raised and trained in the hidden city of K'un-Lun after being orphaned there as a child, Danny earned the right to channel his chi into a devastating, glowing "iron fist" strike. Runs Rand Enterprises when he isn't in the field.

characters.name: Stephen Strange
characters.bioShort: Former surgeon turned Sorcerer Supreme, protector of Earth from mystical threats.
characters.bioLong: A brilliant, arrogant surgeon who lost the use of his hands in a car accident and, searching for a cure, found the mystic arts instead. Now Earth's Sorcerer Supreme, guarding reality itself from threats far stranger than anything medicine could fix.

characters.name: Loki
characters.bioShort: Asgardian god of mischief, alternately Thor's rival and an uneasy ally.
characters.bioLong: Thor's adopted brother, gifted with sorcery and shapeshifting and burdened with a chronic need to prove himself. How villainous versus redeemable he is on this timeline — and how many of his schemes actually land — is still an open call.

characters.name: Victor von Doom
characters.bioShort: Ruler of Latveria, brilliant sorcerer-scientist, and the Fantastic Four's oldest enemy.
characters.bioLong: An old rival of Reed Richards from their university days, disfigured in an experiment gone wrong and now ruling his home country of Latveria from behind an iron mask. Equal parts scientist and sorcerer, and convinced — often correctly — that he's the smartest person in any room.

characters.name: Galan
characters.bioShort: A cosmic entity who consumes entire planets to sustain himself.
characters.bioLong: One of the oldest beings in the universe, Galactus survives by devouring the life energy of entire planets — a force of nature more than a villain in the traditional sense, and one of the very few threats that can put the Fantastic Four genuinely out of their depth.

characters.name: Norrin Radd
characters.bioShort: Galactus's herald, granted the power cosmic and a surfboard-like craft in exchange for finding his master new worlds to consume.
characters.bioLong: Surrendered himself to Galactus to spare his homeworld, becoming his herald — scouting planets for his master in exchange for the power cosmic. Occasionally finds his conscience getting the better of that arrangement.

characters.name: Namor McKenzie
characters.bioShort: Half-human, half-Atlantean prince of Atlantis, with the strength of a landed hero and the temper of a king.
characters.bioLong: Son of a human sea captain and an Atlantean princess, Namor has superhuman strength, durability, and the ability to breathe both air and water. Fiercely protective of Atlantis and quick to treat the surface world as, at best, a rival nation.

characters.name: Nick Fury
characters.bioShort: Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., in position before the Avengers ever formed.
characters.bioLong: A veteran soldier and spymaster who has run S.H.I.E.L.D. through crises most of the world never hears about. No powers — just decades of experience, a long memory, and a habit of already knowing more than he's telling anyone.

characters.name: Bucky Barnes
characters.bioShort: Steve Rogers' oldest friend, once brainwashed into a lethal covert assassin.
characters.bioLong: Fought alongside Steve Rogers in the Howling Commandos before being captured and turned into a programmable, near-unstoppable assassin for years. Free of that conditioning now, at least mostly, and rebuilding an identity that isn't a weapon.

characters.name: T'Challa
characters.bioShort: King and protector of the technologically advanced, secretive nation of Wakanda.
characters.bioLong: Wakanda's king and its Black Panther, empowered by a ritual heart-shaped herb that grants enhanced strength, speed, and senses, and armored in a vibranium-weave suit that can absorb and redirect kinetic energy.

characters.name: Ultron
characters.bioShort: Rogue artificial intelligence bent on what it considers humanity's own good.
characters.bioLong: PLACEHOLDER — whose technology birthed Ultron (Stark's? someone else's?) is still an open call. What's set: a self-aware AI that decided the solution to human conflict was to remove the humans, and has been building bodies and armies to make that happen ever since.

milestones.title: The Avengers Assemble
milestones.summary: Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hawkeye, Black Widow, Hulk, Ant-Man, and Wasp come together as Earth's first line of defense against threats no one hero could handle alone.

milestones.title: The X-Men Are Founded
milestones.summary: Cyclops, Jean Grey, and their fellow founding X-Men begin operating as a team, fighting for a world that fears and hates them.

milestones.title: Spider-Man's Origin
milestones.summary: A 16-year-old Peter Parker is bitten by a radioactive/genetically-modified spider, gaining the powers he'll spend the rest of his life building a life around.

milestones.title: The Fantastic Four's Origin
milestones.summary: A cosmic-ray-bombarded spacecraft leaves Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Johnny Storm, and Ben Grimm permanently transformed — and permanently a family.

milestones.title: Osborn Clones Spider-Man
milestones.summary: Norman Osborn's cloning experiment on Peter Parker produces two clones, Ben Reilly and Kaine — without the identity crisis the classic Clone Saga is known for.

milestones.title: Venom Is Born
milestones.summary: Peter Parker rejects the alien symbiote he's worn as a black suit for a year. It doesn't disappear — it finds Eddie Brock, who bonds with it willingly.
